requirement: energy_mcp and mcpqa are separate distributions (energy-mcp, mcpqa), each with its own pyproject.toml, installed editable from their src folders in this repo.
mcpqa never imports or depends on energy_mcp: the reusable suite sees only what any MCP server exposes.
Installed versions equal the exact pins in requirements.txt, and the MCP SDK is 2.3.0 with the v2 API (MCPServer, Client) this plan is written against.

Traceability: every test cites a catalogued requirement, every catalogued requirement has a test, catalogue IDs are unique and well-formed, and docs/rtm.* is current (CRLF checkouts and BOM catalogues included).
CI runs the full suite on Ubuntu and Windows with Python 3.12, installs the exact pins, has read-only permissions and never references a secret; repo text files are LF.

Tool calls are checked strictly: an unknown tool is a -32602 protocol error; arguments that break the published inputSchema (wrong type, out of range, missing, unexpected) are a tool execution error naming the field and rule, never echoing what the caller sent (values, unknown keys or names); patterns match as JSON Schema (ECMA-262) does; an unexpected exception is -32603.

The investigate_alert(alert_id) prompt is listed and renders for a known alert; an unknown prompt, a missing or unexpected argument, or an unknown alert is -32602, without echoing caller-chosen names.

The world is built only from a seed: the same seed gives the same world in any process; it has 20 meters at 6 sites, 168 hourly readings per meter from 2026-01-05T00:00:00Z, and 50 alerts; all names are synthetic.

On the seeded world, every tool result has structuredContent valid against its outputSchema and a text copy equal to it, on both revisions; every inputSchema is an object that forbids unknown properties; annotations match behaviour.

Tool results are right against the world: filters, complete and ordered pagination, tampered or forged out-of-range cursors rejected, unknown IDs are tool errors, acknowledgement changes the world and is idempotent, a crash is -32603 without detail.

The reports://{name} template and each report are listed; a report reads back as its file text with text/markdown; an unknown or malformed name is -32602 without echoing it; the report files ship inside the package.

The server runs over stdio and Streamable HTTP (main() binds 127.0.0.1 unless --host says otherwise); on both transports and both revisions it lists the same tools, answers a valid call with schema-valid output, a bad argument with isError, and an unknown tool with -32602.

A real Claude client connects to the server over stdio and calls a tool: a recorded Claude Code transcript in docs/evidence/ shows the MCP tool call and the server's answer for the seeded world, and holds nothing private.

A bearer token is accepted only when it is an RS256 at+jwt signed by the configured key, with the configured issuer and audience, every RFC 9068 required claim, exp/iat/nbf valid on the server's clock without leeway, and well-formed sub and client_id; anything else, including garbage, is rejected without an exception.

Over HTTP, a request without a usable bearer token gets 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer carrying resource_metadata and scope; a missing token has no error code, an invalid or expired one has error="invalid_token"; a call without its scope gets 403 insufficient_scope with the needed scope and resource_metadata; challenges never carry caller text.

RFC 9728 metadata is served without auth at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp with resource, authorization_servers = [issuer], scopes_supported = the four base scopes and bearer_methods_supported = [header].
Every tool, resource read and prompt needs its scope (meters:read, alerts:read, reports:read, alerts:write) on every transport; listing needs none; a refused call never changes the world.
alerts:write:<alert_id> lets a caller acknowledge that alert only; alerts:write covers every alert; a malformed or missing alert_id needs alerts:write.

Without HTTP, the identity comes from ENERGY_MCP_SCOPES (default read-only) and ENERGY_MCP_OPERATOR; unknown scopes or a malformed operator are refused at startup; the acknowledging operator is recorded.
Over HTTP, the caller is the token's principal: a session opened by one principal answers 404 to another, and acknowledge_alert records the token's sub.

Over HTTP, each principal gets limit authenticated requests per window on the server's clock; the next one gets 429 with Retry-After, before scope checks and before the server runs; the window resets on the clock; a new token for the same principal does not reset it; other principals are unaffected.

--transport http will not start without a public key and issuer; a real HTTP server process refuses a request without a token and serves one with a valid token; a real stdio process applies ENERGY_MCP_SCOPES.

energy_mcp answers every stdio line that is not a valid message (-32700 for invalid JSON, -32600 otherwise, with the request's id when it has one) and rejects any cursor on a list method with -32602, where the bare SDK stays silent or ignores the cursor (F-13, F-14).

mcpqa is a pytest plugin that takes --target (a stdio JSON array or command, or an HTTP URL), a bearer token from the variable --token-env names, and --protocol-version; it speaks the protocol with its own client and imports neither mcp nor energy_mcp; a check whose precondition is missing skips as not applicable, with the reason.

On 2025-11-25, initialize returns the requested version, serverInfo and capabilities, and an unknown requested version gets another version the server serves; on 2026-07-28, server/discover lists 2026-07-28 and the capabilities, and an unsupported version is -32022 with supported and requested (HTTP 400).
On 2026-07-28, a request without the _meta envelope is -32602 and, over HTTP, a header that does not match the body is -32020; both HTTP 400.

mcpqa's conformance checks all pass on energy_mcp over stdio and HTTP on both revisions, except checks skipped as not applicable with a listed reason; every check has a broken copy, and each broken copy fails exactly its checks.
Every declared capability's list method answers and an undeclared one is -32601, on both revisions.
Invalid JSON is -32700 with id null; a non-request is -32600; an unknown method is -32601 (HTTP 404 on 2026-07-28); an unknown tool is -32602; on both revisions and transports.
Every declared list method paginates to an end without repeating an item, and an invalid cursor is -32602.
A 1 MiB string argument gets a clean answer (a result or -32602, never -32603 or silence) and the server keeps answering; over stdio, stdout carries only MCP messages.
